observation_summary: The ChecksumCalculatingInputStream class allowed null parameters to be passed to its constructor, which later caused a NullPointerException when the object was used (e.g., calling getValue()).
hypothesis: The constructor lacked input validation (guards) for the 'checksum' and 'in' parameters, allowing the object to be initialized in an invalid state.
prediction: Adding explicit null checks in the constructor that throw an exception when parameters are null will prevent the object from being created in an invalid state.
experiment_rationale: The fix provided in the bug report explicitly adds 'if (checksum == null)' and 'if (in == null)' checks to the constructor, which is the standard way to implement parameter validation.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing guard/validation check. The constructor was missing checks for null parameters, which is a failure to validate input data. This fits the definition of 'Checking' perfectly.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'Modified the constructor to assure the input parameters are not null.'
Code snippet in bug report: 'if ( checksum == null ){ throw new NullPointerException(...); }'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix happens in the constructor (initialization phase), the root cause is the lack of validation logic (a guard), not an incorrect value assignment.
The class exists and functions correctly for valid inputs; it just lacks a safety check, which is a local procedural fix, not a design-level capability change.
